newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Verdicts in Bahrain coup trial possible soon.
newsitem.headline: Verdicts in Bahrain coup trial possible soon.

text.p: The trial of 81 people accused of involvement in an alleged Iranian-backed plot to topple Bahrain's government entered its second week and lawyers said on Sunday some verdicts could be passed next week.
"The State Security Court is continuing to try the suspects. There is a possibility the court would pass some verdicts next week," one defence lawyer told Reuters.
The lawyers said 59 suspects were appearing in court and the rest were being tried in absentia.

The defendants are accused of joining the military wing of the Bahraini Hizbollah (Party of God), creating an organisation aimed at toppling the government, possessing weapons without permission and contacting a foreign country.
Political parties are banned in Bahrain.
The suspects could face the death penalty if convicted, lawyers say.
Bahrain in June accused Shi'ite Moslem Iran of backing an attempt to topple the government.

Iran denied the allegation and said it was not interfering in the internal affairs of Bahrain, where members of the island's majority Shi'ite Moslem community demanding political and economic reform by the Sunni rulers have waged a campaign of bombings, arson attacks, sabotage and riots since December 1994.
At least 28 people have been killed and hundreds arrested since.
